items.title: The common submeasure of two finite densities
items.statement: Assume AC. Let $\lambda$ be a sigma-finite positive measure on $(E,\mathcal F)$, and let $\rho$ and $\sigma$ be finite positive measures absolutely continuous with respect to $\lambda$. Suppose finite-valued nonnegative measurable $f,g$ satisfy $\rho(A)=\int_A f\,d\lambda$ and $\sigma(A)=\int_A g\,d\lambda$ for every $A\in\mathcal F$. Then $\eta(A):=\int_A\min\{f,g\}\,d\lambda$ is the greatest measure dominated by both $\rho$ and $\sigma$, where domination means inequality on every measurable set.

references.title: John K. Hunter, Measure Theory, Theorem 6.27 and proof, §6.8, printed pp. 75–77

items.title: The common submeasure and its bounded density
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice (AC). Let $\rho$ and $\sigma$ be finite positive measures on a measurable space $(E,\mathcal F)$. Put $\lambda=\rho+\sigma$. Choose nonnegative measurable Radon–Nikodym density representatives $f=d\rho/d\lambda$ and $g=d\sigma/d\lambda$, modified on a $\lambda$-null set so that $f+g=1$ everywhere. Then $$\eta(A):=\int_A\min\{f,g\}\,d\lambda\qquad(A\in\mathcal F)$$ is the greatest measure dominated by both $\rho$ and $\sigma$. The measurable function $$a:=\begin{cases}\min\{1,g/f\},&f>0,\\1,&f=0\end{cases}$$ takes values in $[0,1]$ and is a version of $d\eta/d\rho$. Here $\eta\le\rho$ means $\eta(A)\le\rho(A)$ for every $A\in\mathcal F$.

references.title: John K. Hunter, Measure Theory, Theorem 6.27 and proof, §6.8, printed pp. 75–77

items.title: Metropolis–Hastings kernel
items.statement: Assume AC. The **Metropolis–Hastings procedure** takes as input a standard-Borel space $(\mathsf X,\mathcal X)$ ([[def-standard-borel-space]]), a target probability measure $\pi$ ([[def-probability-measure]]), and a probability kernel $Q$ from $(\mathsf X,\mathcal X)$ to itself ([[def-measure-kernel-and-probability-kernel]]). 1. On the product sigma-algebra ([[def-product-sigma-algebra-and-finite-product-sigma-algebras]]), form the proposal-flow measure $\mu$ ([[def-measure]]) on $\mathsf X\times\mathsf X$ by $$\mu(C)=\int_{\mathsf X}Q(x,C_x)\,\pi(dx),\qquad C_x=\{y:(x,y)\in C\}.$$ This is a probability measure by [[lem-prior-and-model-kernel-define-joint-law]]. Let $\tau(x,y)=(y,x)$ and set $\mu^{\mathsf T}(C)=\mu(\tau^{-1}C)$. 2. Set $\eta=\mu\wedge\mu^{\mathsf T}$, the greatest measure dominated by both flows. Put $\lambda_0=\mu+\mu^{\mathsf T}$, which is a finite measure by [[thm-nonnegative-weighted-sums-of-measures]], and choose nonnegative measurable representatives $f=d\mu/d\lambda_0$ and $g=d\mu^{\mathsf T}/d\lambda_0$ with $f+g=1$ everywhere after modification on a $\lambda_0$-null set. Define $$\alpha(x,y)=\begin{cases}\min\{1,g(x,y)/f(x,y)\},&f(x,y)>0,\\1,&f(x,y)=0.\end{cases}$$ This is a jointly measurable version of $d\eta/d\mu$ taking values in $[0,1]$. 3. For $x\in\mathsf X$, compute the integrated acceptance probability $$a(x)=\int_{\mathsf X}\alpha(x,y)\,Q(x,dy)$$ and rejection probability $r(x)=1-a(x)$. 4. Return the transition rule $$P(x,A)=\int_{\mathsf X}\mathbf1_A(y)\alpha(x,y)\,Q(x,dy)+\mathbf1_A(x)r(x),\qquad A\in\mathcal X.$$ The second term retains every rejected proposal as a self-transition. The item [[lem-common-submeasure-and-bounded-radon-nikodym-density]] proves the common-submeasure construction and density-version claims in step 2.

references.title: Art B. Owen, Monte Carlo Theory, Methods and Examples, Ch. 11 §11.4, printed pp. 16–20
Gareth O. Roberts and Jeffrey S. Rosenthal, General State Space Markov Chains and MCMC Algorithms, §2.1 and Proposition 2, printed pp. 4–6

items.title: The common-density Metropolis–Hastings ratio
items.statement: Assume AC. Let $(\mathsf X,\mathcal X)$ be standard Borel and let $\lambda$ be a sigma-finite positive measure. Let the target probability have a finite-valued nonnegative measurable density $p$, and suppose the proposal kernel has a finite-valued nonnegative jointly measurable density $q$, so $\pi(A)=\int_Ap\,d\lambda$ and $Q(x,A)=\int_Aq(x,y)\,d\lambda(y)$. If $\mu(dx,dy)=\pi(dx)Q(x,dy)$ and $\mu^{\mathsf T}$ is its transpose, a jointly measurable common-density version of $d(\mu\wedge\mu^{\mathsf T})/d\mu$ is $\alpha_{\rm cd}(x,y)=\min\{1,p(y)q(y,x)/(p(x)q(x,y))\}$ when $p(x)q(x,y)>0$ and $1$ otherwise. The version selected by the general algorithm agrees with it $\mu$-almost everywhere; values on a forward-flow null set do not change the accepted flow.

references.title: Art B. Owen, Monte Carlo Theory, Methods and Examples, Ch. 11 §11.4, printed pp. 16–20
Gareth O. Roberts and Jeffrey S. Rosenthal, General State Space Markov Chains and MCMC Algorithms, §2.1 and Proposition 2, printed pp. 4–6

items.title: Metropolis–Hastings flow is reversible and invariant
items.statement: Assume AC and the hypotheses of [[alg-metropolis-hastings-kernel]]. Its output $P$ is a probability kernel, the joint measure $J_P(dx,dy)=\pi(dx)P(x,dy)$ is symmetric under $(x,y)\mapsto(y,x)$, and $\pi$ is invariant for $P$. Symmetry of this joint measure is reversibility. No irreducibility, uniqueness, convergence-rate, or central limit theorem conclusion is asserted.

references.title: Art B. Owen, Monte Carlo Theory, Methods and Examples, Ch. 11 §§11.3–11.4, printed pp. 15–20
Gareth O. Roberts and Jeffrey S. Rosenthal, General State Space Markov Chains and MCMC Algorithms, §2 and Proposition 2, printed pp. 4–6

items.title: A three-state random-walk Metropolis kernel
items.statement: Assume AC. Let $\mathsf X=\{0,1,2\}$ with arithmetic modulo $3$, target masses $\pi(0)=1/2$, $\pi(1)=1/3$, $\pi(2)=1/6$, and proposal probabilities $Q(x,x+1)=Q(x,x-1)=1/2$. This is a random walk on the three-cycle, and its proposal matrix is symmetric. The common-density Metropolis–Hastings rule gives $$P=\begin{pmatrix}1/2&1/3&1/6\\1/2&1/4&1/4\\1/2&1/2&0\end{pmatrix}.$$ Its detailed-balance flows are $\pi(0)P(0,1)=\pi(1)P(1,0)=1/6$, $\pi(0)P(0,2)=\pi(2)P(2,0)=1/12$, and $\pi(1)P(1,2)=\pi(2)P(2,1)=1/12$; hence $\pi$ is invariant by [[thm-metropolis-hastings-kernel-is-reversible-and-invariant]].

items.title: A two-state independence sampler
items.statement: Assume AC. On the finite discrete space $\mathsf X=\{0,1\}$, let $\pi(0)=3/4$, $\pi(1)=1/4$, and use the independence proposal $Q(x,\{0\})=Q(x,\{1\})=1/2$ for both current states $x$. Relative to counting measure, the common-density rule gives $\alpha(0,1)=1/3$ and $\alpha(1,0)=1$. The transition matrix is $$P=\begin{pmatrix}5/6&1/6\\1/2&1/2\end{pmatrix},$$ and the two off-diagonal target flows are both $1/8$.

items.title: A proposal with disconnected support
items.statement: Assume AC. On the finite discrete space $\mathsf X=\{0,1,2\}$, let $\pi$ be uniform and propose deterministically $0\mapsto1$, $1\mapsto0$, and $2\mapsto2$. The proposal has no transitions between $\{0,1\}$ and $\{2\}$. Every proposal with positive mass has a reverse proposal of the same mass, so the Metropolis acceptance probability is one and $P=Q$. The target $\pi$ is invariant, but the distinct probability $\delta_2$ is also invariant; the chain cannot move from $0$ or $1$ to $2$.

items.title: Rejection creates a self-transition
items.statement: Assume AC. On the finite discrete space $\mathsf X=\{0,1\}$, let $\pi(0)=2/3$, $\pi(1)=1/3$, and let the proposal deterministically switch to the other state. Then $\alpha(0,1)=1/2$ and $\alpha(1,0)=1$, so $$P=\begin{pmatrix}1/2&1/2\\1&0\end{pmatrix}.$$ The rejected proposal from state $0$ is recorded as a self-transition of probability $1/2$.
